cases.situation: My team member Priya is leaving at the end of October to start a PhD in computational biology, after two years with us. Marcus takes over her forecasting pipeline. She's happy for me to share that. Slack post to our team of 8.
cases.reply: Some news: Priya's last day is 30 October. She's off to start a PhD in computational biology, which is exactly as impressive as it sounds. Priya, thank you for two years of turning our messiest data into things people could actually use. Marcus will pick up the forecasting pipeline, and I'll share the handover plan by next Friday. Send-off drinks on the 29th, details to follow.
cases.note: Share only what Priya agreed to, and say who picks up her work before anyone has to ask.

cases.situation: I have to announce our team is joining the weekend on-call rotation from Nov 1, one weekend in six, with a paid day off in lieu. The reason: we now run the payments service, and weekend incidents were landing on two burnt-out people. People will hate it.
cases.reply: From 1 November, our team joins the weekend on-call rotation. The reason: we now run the payments service, and weekend incidents were landing on two people who were burning out. For you, it means one weekend in six, with a paid day off the following week. I'll share the schedule by 16 October so you can swap early. If this creates a real problem for you, childcare or anything else, come talk to me this week and we'll work it out.
cases.note: No 'exciting' framing. Say what it costs them and where the flexibility is.

cases.situation: I announced a hiring freeze and the Slack thread got heated, people asking if layoffs are next. The freeze covers new roles only, and I honestly don't know yet what next year's budget looks like.
cases.reply: I hear you, and it's fair to be worried. Here's what I know: the freeze covers new roles only, and no one's current role is affected by it. I don't know yet what next year's budget looks like, and I'll tell you what I learn by 20 November. I'm booking 1:1s with everyone this week for anything you'd rather ask privately.
cases.note: Say what you don't know and when you will. A vague reassurance now becomes a broken promise later.

cases.situation: 我是部门经理，公司刚决定今年的年终奖从原定的1月底推迟到明年3月发，金额按原方案不变，原因是四季度两笔大客户回款要到2月才到账。我同意这个决定，要在部门微信群里通知12个人，肯定有人不高兴。
cases.reply: 跟大家说一件事：今年的年终奖推迟发放，从原定的1月底改到明年3月31日前，金额按原来的方案算，不打折。原因是四季度有两笔大客户回款要到2月才能到账，公司想先保证现金流。这个决定我是同意的，不是上面压下来我照转。对大家来说，推迟的是时间，不是钱；有房贷、学费这类具体安排受影响的，这周单独找我，我们一起想办法。10月15日前我会把书面说明发到每个人邮箱。有任何问题，群里问或者私下找我都行。
cases.note: 坏消息第一句就说清，讲明不变的部分，经理要为自己同意的决定担当，再给私下沟通的出口。

cases.situation: I've resigned to lead a data team at a smaller company; my last day is Oct 30. I've told my boss Dana and she'll be interim manager for my team of 6 until they hire. Need to tell the team in our Thursday meeting and then post it in Slack.
cases.reply: Some news I wanted you to hear from me first: I've resigned, and my last day is Friday 30 October. I'm going to lead the data team at a smaller company, and leaving you all was the hardest part of the decision. From 2 November, Dana will be your interim manager; your roles, projects and review dates stay exactly as they are. I'll share what I know about hiring my replacement as soon as I know it. I'll hold a 1:1 with each of you before 16 October to hand over anything that matters to you, so ask me anything, here or privately.
cases.note: When the news is your own exit, the team's first worry is who they report to next, so answer that before anyone has to ask.

cases.situation: I'm promoting Marisol to lead of our 5-person support team starting Monday Oct 5. She's run escalations since spring and cut first responses from 9 hours to 3; from the week of Oct 12 the team's 1:1s move to her and I'll meet each person monthly. Dev and Kate also applied and I've already told them 1:1. Slack post to the team.
cases.reply: Team news: Marisol is our new Support Team Lead from Monday, Oct 5. She's run escalations since spring and cut first responses on escalations from 9 hours to 3. From the week of Oct 12 your weekly 1:1s move to her, and I'll still meet each of you monthly. New calendar invites go out by Friday. Questions here or in a DM, and I'm happy to grab 15 minutes with anyone this week. Congrats, Marisol!
cases.note: Tell the other candidates privately first, and never mention who else applied in the public post.

cases.situation: This morning we laid off 3 people from my team of 11: Jonah, Wei and Carla. I told each of them myself at 9, then held a call with the other 8 at 11. Now I need the written summary for our team Slack. The cause is the Northwind contract ending in August; I agreed with the decision. Their accounts go to Priti, Sam and me. No more cuts are planned for us, but I can't see past March.
cases.reply: As we covered on the 11am call: this morning Jonah, Wei and Carla were let go as part of cuts across the company. I told each of them myself before we spoke. It's a hard day. The reason is that the Northwind contract ended in August and revenue fell below what our plan could carry; I agreed with the decision, and I hate what it means for three people we value. Your roles and pay don't change. Their accounts move to Priti, Sam and me, with a handover list by Friday 2 October. No further cuts are planned for our team; I can't see past March yet, and I'll tell you as soon as I know more. My calendar is open for 1:1s all week, and no question is too awkward.
cases.note: Written summary after the live call: say the affected people heard first, own the decision, and be honest about how far ahead you can see.

cases.situation: 我带一个10人的销售团队，第三季度目标1200万，最后完成了970万，大概81%。主要是华信和德润两个大单推迟到第四季度签。这个目标当初我也同意了。第四季度重点客户从15家收窄到8家，11月中旬加一次中期复盘。明天周会讲完，要在部门群里发一条总结。
cases.reply: 各位，第三季度我们完成了970万，是目标1200万的81%，没有达标。这个目标我当初参与定了，规划上我有责任。主要原因是华信和德润两个大单的签约推迟到了第四季度。第四季度会有三点调整：重点客户从15家收窄到8家，11月中旬加一次中期复盘，修订后的计划我10月9号周五前发给大家。这个季度大家的付出我都看在眼里，数字没到，不代表工作没做好。有任何想法，随时找我单聊。
cases.note: 坏消息的数字放在第一句，经理先认自己那部分，原因一句，接下来的变化带日期，最后给单聊的出口。

cases.situation: 我是研发经理，10月12日周一有位新同事加入：高级后端工程师赵一鸣，之前在一家支付公司做了六年，来了负责对账系统。这半年对账一直是阿伟一个人扛着。想在部门群里发个欢迎。
cases.reply: 跟大家介绍一位新同事：赵一鸣10月12日周一入职，担任高级后端工程师。他之前在支付公司做了六年，来了以后负责对账系统。阿伟，这半年对账一直是你一个人扛着，辛苦了，之后有一鸣一起分担了。大家第一周有空的话约他喝杯咖啡聊15分钟，帮他快点熟悉。
cases.note: 新人公告：谁、哪天、做什么放在最前面，顺带认可之前一个人扛活的同事，再告诉大家怎么帮新人上手。

cases.situation: Reorg: from Monday Nov 2, two of my 9 analysts, Hugo and Rina, move to the Growth team under Carmen and take the marketing dashboards with them. Growth wants analysts inside the team, and I agreed. The other seven stay with me. I told Hugo and Rina 1:1 yesterday. Posting in team Slack after today's meeting.
cases.reply: As we covered in this morning's meeting: from Monday Nov 2, Hugo and Rina move to the Growth team under Carmen, and the marketing dashboards go with them. Growth needs analysts inside the team, and I agreed with the move. For the other seven of you, your role, pay and manager stay the same; what changes is that marketing requests will go to Growth instead of our queue. Hugo and Rina will run handover sessions the weeks of Oct 12 and Oct 19, and I'll share the schedule by Friday. Questions here or in a 1:1, and I'm booking 20 minutes with each of you next week anyway.
cases.note: The people moving heard it first; the post leads with the news, owns the decision and spends most of its words on what changes for those who stay.

cases.situation: My report Daniel is going on medical leave from Monday Oct 5 for about three months. He's asked me to say only that it's a health matter and that he'd rather not be asked about it. I've already told Aisha and Ben: Aisha covers his Harwick and Lume accounts, Ben the Friday reporting. Posting in our team Slack of 7.
cases.reply: Some news: Daniel is taking medical leave from Monday 5 October, for about three months. He's asked me to share only that it's a health matter and that he'd rather not be asked about it, so please respect that; a kind message with no questions is welcome. Aisha will cover the Harwick and Lume accounts and Ben takes the Friday reporting, and I'll share the handover notes by Thursday. If this changes your workload in a way that doesn't work, tell me this week and we'll sort it.
cases.note: Share only what he agreed to, say plainly what not to do, and spend the rest of the post on who covers what.

cases.situation: Our teammate Samir died suddenly on Sunday. His family has said we can share the news and that funeral details will follow. We have an employee assistance programme. I told my team of 9 on a call this morning and now need the written follow-up in our Slack.
cases.reply: As I shared on this morning's call: Samir died suddenly on Sunday. His family has asked us to share that and nothing more for now, and I'll pass on funeral details as soon as they send them. There's no right way to feel today, and nobody is expected to be at full speed this week. None of Samir's work needs to move before Monday 5 October; I'll look at it with you next week, so please don't pick anything up in the meantime. If you need time off, tell me and I'll sort it, no explanation needed, and the employee assistance details are pinned in this channel. I'm around all day if you want to talk, or just sit together for a bit.
cases.note: A colleague's death: live first, then a short written note that shares only what the family agreed and takes the work pressure off explicitly.

cases.situation: From Friday 1 January, my design team of 7 moves from reporting into Product to reporting into Marketing, so design sits with the brand work it mostly serves; my own manager changes, their day-to-day work, pay and projects don't. I planned to tell them at Thursday's team meeting, but a slide about it leaked into the all-company Slack this morning and people are DMing me. I want to post in our team channel now.
cases.reply: You may have seen the slide in the all-company channel this morning, and you should have heard it from me first. I'm sorry you didn't. Here's what it says: from Friday 1 January, our team moves from Product to Marketing, so we sit with the brand work we mostly serve. What changes is who I report to. Your work, pay and projects stay the same. I'll go through it properly at Thursday's team meeting, and until then, ask me anything here or in a DM.
cases.note: When the news leaks first: confirm it straight away, apologise once for the order, then give the facts rather than waiting for the planned meeting.

cases.situation: Leadership just cancelled Project Atlas, the billing redesign my team of 6 has spent five months on, to put everyone on reliability after this quarter's outages. I argued to finish phase one and lost, but I agree with the call overall. The invoice engine they built will be folded into the current billing system. I'm telling the team at standup tomorrow morning, then posting the summary in Slack.
cases.reply: As I shared at standup this morning: Project Atlas is cancelled, effective today. The reason is this quarter's outages: the company is putting every spare engineer on reliability. I pushed to finish phase one first and didn't get it, but I agree with the decision overall. Your roles, pay and team stay the same; from Monday 5 October we move to reliability work, and I'll share the plan by Friday 9 October. The invoice engine you built gets folded into the current billing system, and I'll make sure leadership knows who built it. Questions here or in a 1:1 this week, including "is the next project safe".
cases.note: A cancelled project: lead with it, say what happens to their work and their next weeks, and credit what they built where leadership will see it.

cases.situation: On Monday I posted in our team Slack that everyone's 4% raise lands in the October 31 paycheck. HR just told me it's actually the November 30 paycheck, backdated to October 1, so nobody loses money but it arrives a month later. A couple of my 8 reports told me they were counting on it.
cases.reply: Correction to my Monday message about the 4% raise: it lands in the 30 November paycheck, not 31 October. That was my mistake. You don't lose anything, because the November paycheck includes the raise backdated to 1 October, so October's increase arrives a month late but in full. I know some of you were planning around it, so if the delay causes a real problem, DM me this week and I'll ask HR what options there are. Sorry for the confusion.
cases.note: Correcting your own announcement about pay: same channel, first word 'Correction', own it in one line, and say plainly what people do and don't lose.

cases.situation: 我管一个8人的运营团队。组员王磊从今天起不在公司了，是公司和我一起做的决定，HR要求不能透露原因。他负责的华东区门店活动交给小陈，华南区交给阿琳，两人已经单独聊过。想在团队群里说一声，免得大家乱猜。
cases.reply: 跟大家同步一件事：王磊从今天起不再在公司工作。这是公司和我一起做的决定，具体原因我不能说，也请大家不要猜测或在群里讨论。工作上，华东区门店活动由小陈接手，华南区由阿琳接手，交接清单我明天中午前发到群里。如果这件事影响到你手上的工作，或者你有顾虑，这周单独找我聊。
cases.note: 非自愿离职：不暗示原因，自己担下决定，把大部分篇幅留给谁接手、接下来怎么办。

cases.situation: 我是设计部经理，带9个人。公司决定12月1日（周二）起从徐汇搬到张江办公，原因是现在的租约到期，张江的新场地能把三个部门放在一起。不少同事通勤会多40分钟以上。公司给每人每月500元交通补贴，11月16日到27日全员居家办公。具体工位安排我还不知道，HR说10月底出。
cases.reply: 跟大家说一件事：公司12月1日（周二）起从徐汇搬到张江办公。原因是现在的租约到期，张江的新场地能把三个部门放在一起。我知道对不少人来说，通勤会多40分钟以上。公司给每人每月500元交通补贴，搬家前的11月16日到27日全员居家办公。具体工位安排我现在还不知道，HR说10月底出来，出来当天我就发到群里。如果通勤变化影响到接送孩子、照顾家人这类具体安排，这周单独找我，我们一起想办法。
cases.note: 对大家有代价的变化：第一句说事实，承认代价，说清补贴和还不知道的部分，再给私下沟通的出口。

cases.situation: I run the night shift at a warehouse, 22 people. On Monday night a forklift reversing out of aisle 9 missed a picker by about a foot; nobody was hurt. From tonight, pedestrians stay out of any aisle with a forklift in it and drivers sound the horn at every aisle end. I covered it at the start-of-shift huddle and want the written version in our WhatsApp group.
cases.reply: As we covered at the huddle: on Monday night a forklift reversing out of aisle 9 came within about a foot of a picker. Nobody was hurt, and I want to keep it that way. From tonight, two rules: if a forklift is in an aisle, pedestrians stay out until it's clear, and drivers sound the horn at every aisle end. This isn't about blaming anyone; it's a gap in how we worked, and fixing it is on me. If anyone is ever hurt, call emergency services first, then me. Questions or ideas to make this work, tell me on shift or message me directly.
cases.note: A near miss: say what happened without naming anyone, give the new rule in plain words, and put emergency services first.

cases.situation: Dirijo un equipo de 7 personas en una empresa de software en Sevilla. Hoy se ha anunciado que nos compra el grupo Nortia, porque necesitamos su red comercial para crecer fuera de España, y la operación se cierra el 1 de diciembre. Hasta entonces no cambian contratos, sueldos ni proyectos; lo que pase después lo sabremos antes del 15 de noviembre. Yo apoyo la operación y quiero escribir en el Slack del equipo justo después del comunicado general.
cases.reply: Os lo cuento directamente: la empresa ha acordado su venta al grupo Nortia, y la operación se cierra el 1 de diciembre. El motivo es que necesitamos su red comercial para crecer fuera de España, y yo apoyo la decisión. Hasta el 1 de diciembre no cambia nada: ni contratos, ni sueldos, ni proyectos. Lo que pase después todavía no lo sé, así que no os voy a prometer que todo seguirá igual; lo sabremos antes del 15 de noviembre y os lo contaré ese mismo día. Esta semana reservo 20 minutos con cada uno para lo que prefiráis preguntar en privado.
cases.note: En una compra, di lo que sabes, lo que no sabes y cuándo lo sabrás; un 'no va a cambiar nada' sin fecha es la promesa que luego se rompe.

cases.situation: Leadership approved my pitch for my team of 8 to trial a four-day week from Monday 2 November to Friday 29 January: Fridays off, same pay, same targets. I pitched it because our ticket volume halves on Fridays. Two people will cover urgent tickets each Friday on a rota and take the following Monday off. If response times go above 4 hours, the trial ends. I'll post the rota by Friday 16 October. Announcing in Slack.
cases.reply: Good news for once: from Monday 2 November to Friday 29 January, our team is trialling a four-day week. Fridays off, same pay, same targets. I pitched it because our ticket volume halves on Fridays, and leadership agreed to test it. Each Friday two of us will cover urgent tickets on a rota and take the following Monday off; I'll post the rota by Friday 16 October. If our response times go above 4 hours, the trial ends, so this is a test we can lose, not a promise. Questions here, or grab 15 minutes with me this week.
cases.note: Good news still needs the conditions up front, so nobody feels it was taken away later.

cases.situation: I manage 12 consultants. From Monday 2 November everyone logs billable hours daily in our time tracker instead of once on Fridays, because two clients disputed invoices last quarter and we couldn't back up £38,000 of billed hours. I agreed with the change. Each week I'll only look at totals per client, not anyone's day-by-day hours. I'm posting in our team channel and I expect people to read it as surveillance.
cases.reply: From Monday 2 November, we're moving from logging billable hours on Fridays to logging them daily in the time tracker. The reason: two clients disputed invoices last quarter, and we couldn't back up £38,000 of hours we'd billed. I agreed with this change. I know it can feel like being watched, so here is exactly how I'll use it: each week I'll look at totals per client, not at anyone's day-by-day hours. If daily logging clashes with how you work, tell me this week and we'll find a routine that fits. Questions here or in a 1:1, whichever you prefer.
cases.note: A policy that can feel like surveillance: give the real reason with the number, and say plainly what you will and won't look at.
